claims.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
claims.evidence: For an explicitly represented board and piece sequence, a fixed-orientation domino has only O(WH) legal translations, plus constant-size spawn/loss state. Given one certified lock translation per piece, breadth-first search decides its reachability in this finite graph and checks that downward motion is blocked. The verifier can then apply the lock, source-defined loss test, and deterministic row deletion in polynomial time. Any reachable translation has a simple path, so cycles do not enlarge the certificate beyond polynomial size.
claims.search_method: Direct polynomial-verifier and finite-state reachability proof for the source's explicitly listed finite sequence model.

claims.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
claims.evidence: Track each row as a token. Until an initial token clears, its initially filled cells persist and separate its initially empty intervals, so interval length l accepts at most floor(l/2) horizontal dominoes. Such a token can clear only when every empty interval has even length. Thus initial tokens accept at most C pieces and at most q of them can be deleted. Each deletion creates one empty odd-width token; its occupancy remains even after every horizontal lock, so it can never attain the odd full-row occupancy and accepts at most floor(W/2) pieces. Hence U=C+q floor(W/2) is valid. Since C and q are obtained by one board scan and U<=2H floor(W/2)=H(W-1), the claimed computable linear bound follows.
claims.witness: The invariant yields U=C+q floor(W/2), where C is the sum of interval capacities and q counts initial rows whose empty intervals all have even length.
claims.search_method: Direct row-token invariant proof, supplemented by exhaustive exact state search over 123792 stable odd-width board/spawn instances for W in {3,5} and H in {2,3}.

claims.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
claims.evidence: Partition the even width into adjacent pairs. With two empty top rows, a straight-dropped domino over any pair lands below the top row and caps both columns at the same height. If no row clears while every pair is capped, let T be the maximum cap height and keep dropping on lower pairs until all reach T; every lock remains below the top row and the empty top-row corridor supplies reachability. The last pair reaching T completes that row, unless an earlier placement already caused a clear. Any clear inserts an empty top row and shifts the previously empty top row down, restoring two empty top rows. Each phase is finite and contains a clear, so it repeats indefinitely.
claims.witness: The repeatable phase caps every fixed column pair, levels all pair tops to their maximum T, clears row T, and restores two empty top rows.
claims.search_method: Direct constructive invariant proof, supplemented by exact simulation of five consecutive clearing phases for 1039 even-width board/spawn instances with widths 2, 4, and 6.

claims.claim: On an initially empty odd-width W×H board, a row-parallel unrotatable-domino play has no row clears and can survive at most H floor(W/2) pieces; this upper bound need not be attained.
claims.evidence: Before a hypothetical first clear, every row has even occupancy because it starts empty and each horizontal lock adds two cells to one row. A full odd-width row has odd occupancy, so no first clear exists. Without clears, each row contains at most floor(W/2) disjoint dominoes, giving H floor(W/2). Exact reachability enumeration confirms that on the empty 3×2 board the first piece can lock safely only on the bottom row; thereafter every horizontal position is supported into the top row, and every top-row position intersects either possible adjacent spawn pair. Thus the exact safe maximum is 1, strictly below the bound 2.
claims.witness: Empty 3×2 board: maximum safe length 1 for either possible adjacent top-row spawn pair, versus H floor(W/2)=2.
claims.search_method: Parity proof plus exhaustive integer-bitmask reachability and safe-lock enumeration; also checked the no-clear invariant on empty odd boards of widths 3 and 5 and heights 2 and 3.

claims.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
claims.evidence: For the 3×3 board top/middle/bottom .../.#./..., the token formula gives U=2, but every horizontal placement contains the middle column. The obstruction therefore supports the first piece in the top row, where either possible position intersects either adjacent spawn pair and loses; the exact maximum is 0. For the 3×2 board .../..#, the first domino fills and clears the bottom row, leaving the empty 3×2 board. That empty board admits exactly one further safe lock, so the original position has finite maximum 2 despite achieving a row clear. These respectively disprove sufficiency of the capacity bound and any general clear-once implication.
claims.witness: Exact witnesses: .../.#./... on 3×3 has U=2 but maximum 0; .../..# on 3×2 clears once but has maximum safe length 2.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive finite-state enumeration for both possible adjacent width-3 spawn pairs, including movement reachability, blocked-down locking, spawn overlap, and row deletion.
